text:
Alex: CI turned red on main after the toolchain image roll (gcc13 -> gcc14). Lots of compile failures referencing private headers that used to be reachable. Anyone else seeing this?
Priya: yep, saw ~20 targets fail in the linux and mac smoke shards. error looks like: 
```
fatal error: 'third_party/somelib/internal/private.h' file not found
```
Alex: interesting — those were internal headers, we shouldn't be including them directly. But the change in include paths from the new sysroot image seems to have exposed it.
CI-bot: Build shard linux-smoke-12 failed (flaky: false). https://ci.example.com/build/45321
Jamie: quick triage: can someone try rerunning the failing shard with the previous image? if it passes, it's almost certainly the image bump.
Todd: I can kick one off. rerunning linux-smoke-12 with toolchain-image: gcc13-2025-11-01 now.
Maria: FYI the PR that rolled the image is #1428 (infra/toolchains). cc @Priya for visibility.
Priya: thanks. If the rerun passes, we should bisect the image diff to find which sysroot change broke public include/export paths. For a quick workaround we could add a strict header dep in the offending targets.
Jamie: agree. Also run `bazel query 'deps(//path/to/failing:target)' --output graph` to spot where private headers are pulled in.
Alex: rerun finished: linux-smoke-12 PASSED with gcc13 image. so it's definitely the new image.
Todd: opened an infra bug: infra#284 to track reverting/patching the image. I added the build logs and a sample failing target list.
Maria: can we avoid reverting immediately? maybe add a temporary visibility shim in somelib that re-exports the needed headers as public; less risky than full revert.
Priya: ok I can prototype the shim in a branch and run the full CI. If it fixes things we can merge quickly and continue the image roll.
Jamie: sounds good. For the bisect, @Alex can you grab the image diff/manifest and run binary search? `git bisect` doesn't apply to images but diffing the image build recipe should.
Alex: will do. tagging @eng-infra for any pressure to revert. thanks all, will report back with the offending layer and a minimal repro.
